hypotheses.idea: Standardized downside-tail breadth across contemporaneous index constituents predicts a lower safe crypto gross budget.
Downside commonality: the market component's squared standardized loss divided by mean constituent squared standardized loss predicts crypto stress.
Acceleration in the fraction of constituents below a rolling 10th-percentile standardized return is more informative than its level.
Tail breadth matters only when crypto market realized volatility is also above its own trailing median.
Breadth-price divergence (equity market trend strong while constituent trend breadth deteriorates) is an early risk-off warning for crypto.
Failed recovery after an equity downside shock, measured by short rebound divided by prior shock magnitude, predicts continued crypto fragility.
Correlation snapback (short commonality minus long commonality) identifies transition into systemic rather than idiosyncratic equity stress.
Breadth deterioration is useful only when equity drawdown duration is increasing.
A tiny rolling ridge model of stock market return, breadth, vol term, tail breadth, commonality and dispersion predicts next-session crypto market return sign/magnitude.
A univariate rolling stock-market-return predictor is the non-ML ablation for H09.
Use only the negative part of the rolling ridge forecast to size risk; positive forecasts do not lever beyond unit gross.
Forecast uncertainty from trailing residual error should attenuate the magnitude of the ridge overlay.
Acceleration of average pairwise correlation inferred from cross-sectional standardized returns predicts crypto drawdown risk.
Dispersion collapse concurrent with rising commonality is a stronger systemic-risk state than high correlation alone.
The sign of commonality acceleration matters more than its historical level.
Inverting the correlation-acceleration direction is the destructive falsifier.
Realized-volatility curve curvature across 10/21/63/126 sessions detects transition risk better than a single short/long ratio.
Vol-of-vol acceleration should reduce crypto gross even if the equity market trend remains positive.
Cross-sectional spread in constituent volatility is an uncertainty state distinct from market volatility level.
A plain inverse-vol gross scaler is the mechanism-free ablation.
Disagreement between S&P-500 and Nasdaq-100 turbulence states predicts unstable risk appetite and should attenuate crypto deployment.
Nasdaq stress leading S&P stress by several sessions is an early risk-off warning.
S&P stress leading Nasdaq stress is the symmetric directional alternative, fixed before returns.
Use the maximum of independently normalized S&P and Nasdaq risk states rather than their mean when they disagree.
